{{nihongo|'''Hakken-gū'''|八剣宮}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

'''Hakkengu''' (はっけんぐう) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Q1355625|qid=Q1355625}}, {{ill|Nagoya|Q11751|qid=Q11751}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|Q80434|qid=Q80434}}. It is an auxiliary shrine (bekku) of {{ill|Atsuta Shrine|Q482065|qid=Q482065}} and also a precinct auxiliary shrine. In the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'' it is listed as "Hakken Shrine" in Aichi District, {{ill|Owari Province|Q514506|qid=Q514506}}, and is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}.

=== Enshrined deity ===
=== Principal deity ===
* '''Atsuta Omikami'''
** Identified with '''{{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602}}''', whose {{ill|Shintai|Q327532|qid=Q327532}} is the '''Kusanagi sacred sword''' (also called Kusanagi-no-Tsurugi / Ame-no-Murakumo-no-Tsurugi), one of the {{ill|Imperial Regalia of Japan|Q327465|qid=Q327465}}<ref group="注釈">"Kusanagi sacred sword" is the official name used at Atsuta Jingu.</ref>.

=== History ===
It is said to have been founded in {{ill|708|Q23511|qid=Q23511}} ({{ill|Wadō (era)|Q1373026|qid=Q1373026}} 1), when {{ill|Empress Genmei|Q233224|qid=Q233224}} had a new sacred sword cast and dedicated following the {{ill|theft of Kusanagi no Tsurugi|Q861812|qid=Q861812}}. In the mid-Heian ''Engishiki Jinmyocho,'' it appears as "Hakken Shrine" in Aichi District, Owari Province. Concerning divine rank, the {{ill|Owari Kokunai Jinmyōchō|Q11041830|qid=Q11041830}} in the {{ill|Jōji|Q1146153|qid=Q1146153}} manuscript has "Senior First Rank, Hakken Myojin," and the {{ill|Genki (era)|Q1145064|qid=Q1145064}} manuscript has "Senior First Rank Upper, Haken Daimyojin."

In the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kamakura period}}, it seems to have stood southeast of the Chinno-mon gate of Atsuta Jingu; a record in the ''Owari Chikatsugu Moshijo-an Dankan'' (compiled around the Bunryaku era) notes a {{ill|Conflagration|Q168983|qid=Q168983}} together with Hiwari-no-miya. In the ''{{ill|Azuma Kagami|Q1042324|qid=Q1042324}}'' entry for {{ill|1180|Q19702|qid=Q19702}} ({{ill|Jishō|Q1194671|qid=Q1194671}} 4), it appears as "Atsuta Hakken." In the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}} it was called "Hakken Myojin" or "Hakken Daimyojin" and stood slightly east of its current location. Records include reconstruction of the main hall by {{ill|Tokugawa Tsunayoshi|Q313745|qid=Q313745}} in {{ill|1686|Q7664|qid=Q7664}} ({{ill|Jōkyō|Q1146221|qid=Q1146221}} 3).

In {{ill|1880|Q7806|qid=Q7806}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 13), it was renamed the auxiliary shrine "Hakkengu." During shrine rebuilding in {{ill|1893|Q7840|qid=Q7840}} (Meiji 26), it moved to the current site. Its architectural style, annual festivals, and rites are all conducted in accordance with the main sanctuary of Atsuta Jingu.

[[File:Atsuta Hongu oyobi Setsu-Matsu-sha no Zu.png|thumb|right|250px|Layout of Atsuta Jingu auxiliary shrines in the late Edo period]]

=== Location ===
* {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|Q80434|qid=Q80434}}{{ill|Nagoya|Q11751|qid=Q11751}}{{ill|Atsuta-ku, Nagoya|Q1355625|qid=Q1355625}}{{ill|Jingū|Q30934394|qid=Q30934394|lt=Jingu}}1-1-1, within the grounds of Atsuta Jingu.

=== Access ===
All are within walking distance.

=== Rail ===
* Nearest to the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=main gate}} (south gate): {{ill|Nagoya Municipal Subway|Q1144874|qid=Q1144874}}{{ill|Meijō Line|Q906775|qid=Q906775|lt=Meijo Line}} {{ill|Atsuta Jingu Temma-cho Station|Q970033|qid=Q970033}}, Exit 1.
* {{ill|Meitetsu|Q30850|qid=Q30850|lt=Meitetsu}} {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Q1137838|qid=Q1137838|lt=Nagoya Main Line}} / {{ill|Meitetsu Tokoname Line|Q6810420|qid=Q6810420|lt=Tokoname Line}} {{ill|Jingū-mae Station|Q6202481|qid=Q6202481}}.
* Nagoya Municipal Subway Meijo Line {{ill|Atsuta Jingu Nishi Station|Q903638|qid=Q903638}}.
* {{ill|Central Japan Railway Company|Q513679|qid=Q513679|lt=JR}} {{ill|Tōkaidō Line (JR Central)|Q11235139|qid=Q11235139|lt=Tokaido Main Line}} {{ill|Atsuta Station|Q871814|qid=Q871814}}.

=== Bus ===
* {{ill|Nagoya Municipal Bus|Q11414982|qid=Q11414982}} - get off at "Jingu Higashimon," "Atsuta Temmacho," "Atsuta Eki Nishi," "Atsuta Kuyakusho," or "Meitetsu Jingumae" stops; all are a short walk.

=== By car ===
* Parking available. During the first three days of New Year (January 1-3), parking is for related personnel only.

=== Nearby ===
* {{ill|Miya-juku|Q3033374|qid=Q3033374}} - 41st {{ill|Shukuba|Q1209783|qid=Q1209783}} on the {{ill|53 Stations of the Tōkaidō|Q3134262|qid=Q3134262}}; the temple-town of Atsuta Jingu.
* {{ill|Shiratori Kofun (Nagoya)|Q11580543|qid=Q11580543|lt=Shiratori Kofun}} - said to be the mausoleum of Yamato Takeru.
* {{ill|Danpusan Kofun|Q5221001|qid=Q5221001}} - largest {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|Q11268718|qid=Q11268718}} in the Tokai region; said to be the tomb of Miyasu-hime.
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Matsuga Shrine}} - auxiliary shrine of Atsuta Jingu, along {{ill|Japan National Route 1|Q1191191|qid=Q1191191}} near Atsuta Jingu's main gate.
